title: Contrastive learning
reading: The slide states the core objective of contrastive learning: pull positive pairs together in embedding space while pushing negative pairs apart. A schematic below shows the standard siamese setup with weight-shared encoders and a similarity matrix used to compute the loss.

visuals.description: Two green trapezoid encoders (top: 'key image', bottom: 'Query image'), both feeding a 5x5 similarity grid with the diagonal cells highlighted in blue, labelled 'loss'. Red arrows flow back from the loss to both encoders. Annotations: 'Share weights for both encoder' above, 'Update both encoders' below.
visuals.assertion: Key and query images pass through weight-sharing encoders; their embeddings form a similarity matrix whose diagonal entries are the positive pairs, and gradients from the loss update both encoders.

concepts.name: Positive/negative pairs
concepts.why_it_matters: Defines what the contrastive objective maximizes versus minimizes.

concepts.name: Weight sharing (siamese encoders)
concepts.why_it_matters: Ensures both views are embedded in a common space.

concepts.name: Similarity matrix
concepts.why_it_matters: Diagonal = positives, off-diagonal = negatives within a batch.
